page.layout: One printed page (left) with a running head at the top, marginal notes in the left margin, and the main text in one column. The right edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Sed nullum noftrum Opus bonum confi-ftit in Condignitate Æqualitatis Justitiæ ad Præ-mium vitæ æternæ:
Proinde nullum Opus bonum eft Meritori-um de Condigno.

Propositionem Adversarii ipfi ultro nobis porrexerunt: Nihil amplius requiritur ad Con-dignitatem, quàm Æqualitas. Alteram enim Commutativam esse volunt, Distributivam alte-ram. (Supra, Cap.2. per totum.)

head.i: Nullum Opus bonum in alterutra Justitiæ Æqualitate confistere.

main_text.head: SECT. II.
main_text.p: CArdinal. Bellarminus, {f}Debet Deus, Lib. 5. de Justif. cap.14. inquit, reddere vitam æternam ex Justitia Commutativa, vel Distributiva: Ex Commutativa, quoad substantiam; ex Distributiva, quoad modum. Sic ille. Nos verò ex diametro, Nec Commutativa (inquimus) nec Distributiva Justitia proprie intercedit inter Deum & Hominem. Agedùm, sit pedi pes junctus.

1. Commutativam aggredimur; de qua Pontificii sensum suum explicant: inter quos Cofte-rus Jesuita, {e}Commutativa aequalitas est, inquit, Enchirid. Tract. de Meritis, c.7 rei cum re; qualis est in emptionibus, permutationibus,

page.notes: The word "Cap.3" in the running head is hard to read; the numeral may be a 3 written in an old form, so it is marked [?]. The note marks "f" and "e" are small and doubtful. Some italic and roman boundaries in the Bellarminus quotation are uncertain. The line-end word "nibus," is the last line and is taken as a continuation of "permutatio-".
